description: A deliberately small notes CLI. The point of this repository is not what it does, it is that an agent can work in it verifiably.

items.title: Atomic JSON storage
items.description: Read and write notes to a JSON file. A partial write loses every note, not just the one being added.
acceptance: src/storage.py exposes load(path) and save(path, notes)
save() is atomic: temp file on the same filesystem, then rename
load() returns [] when the file does not exist
tests/test_storage.py covers all three, including that no temp file is left behind
items.closed_by: Seeded as already-complete so the example starts with a closed item, and with the ledger row that closing one actually requires.

items.title: Search notes by substring
items.description: `notes search <term>` prints the notes whose title or body contains the term, case-insensitively.
acceptance: `notes search bread` prints notes whose title contains 'bread'
The match is case-insensitive and also looks at the body
A search with no matches prints 'no matches' and exits 0
tests/test_cli.py covers a hit, a case-insensitive hit, a body-only hit, and a miss

items.title: Export notes for another tool to consume
items.description: Something downstream needs the notes. The shape of that contract is the actual decision here, not the code that writes it.
acceptance: `notes export` writes every note to stdout in a documented, stable shape
The shape is versioned so a consumer can detect a breaking change
tests cover the shape itself, not just that the command exits 0
items.decision_required: Is this a stable public contract other tools may depend on, or a convenience dump we are free to change? The two answers produce different work: one needs a version field and a compatibility rule, the other does not.
